And since its setup and maintenance costs are relatively low compared to other networks, it is good to use in small areas like offices or homes. In particular, sharing resources through LAN is possible so devices like scanners, printers or storage media do not need to be individually prepared and devices within the LAN can share and use a single equipment. Lastly, expansion, deletion and movement of devices within the network are simple. Since it is not in a complex form like a distributed network, the advantage is that components can be flexibly changed according to needs.

The switching methods consist of a total of three types: cut-through, interim cut-through, and store-and-forward. The cut-through method is an approach with the advantage of minimizing relay time by reading only the first few bytes without error checking rather than reading the entire bytes of the frame to obtain the transmission and reception addresses of the frame. However, as much as the time is shortened, there is a disadvantage that data accuracy slightly decreases because runt frames and error checking are not performed. The interim cut-through method is an approach that compensates for the disadvantage of not processing runt frames in the cut-through method. The store-and-forward method is an approach that goes through all error processes after storing all frames in the buffer. Nevertheless, there is a disadvantage that the waiting time of the frame becomes long in the process of doing this.

The operational mechanism involves generating a random initialization vector when a client requests AP authentication, which is then retransmitted to the AP using the generated WEP key, establishing a connection upon decrypting the ciphertext with the WEP key and matching it with the initially generated initialization vector. WPA (Wi-Fi Protected Access) was developed to compensate for the security vulnerabilities of WEP while utilizing the TKIP algorithm, and whereas WPA utilizes RC4, WPA2 enhanced encryption further by employing the AES algorithm.
